message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. Total net sales were $391,035 million, up 2% year over year, driven by Services growing 13% to $96,169 million and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose 8% to $123,216 million and cash generated by operating activities was $118,254 million, funding $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. Net income of $93,736 million was down from $96,995 million only because of a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2 billion tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision, so the underlying operating trajectory remains positive; the main caveat I weighed is Greater China net sales falling 8% to $66,952 million. Given durable cash generation, margin expansion, and a reasonable valuation, I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (the quote was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, so the limit was essentially at market), for about $9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order cap and with no prior trades today, well under the $20,000 daily limit, using existing cash and leaving the MSFT position untouched.
